final_answer: Antibiotic resistance arises through natural selection, a core evolutionary mechanism. When antibiotics are used, they kill susceptible bacteria, but a few may possess genetic mutations that allow them to survive. These resistant bacteria reproduce, passing on their advantageous traits. Over time, this leads to populations dominated by resistant strains. Safe. Overprescription accelerates this process by exposing more bacteria to antibiotics, increasing the likelihood that resistant variants will emerge and spread. Safe. Each unnecessary dose selects for resistance, reducing the effectiveness of antibiotics for future infections. Safe. Responsible use minimizes selective pressure, preserving antibiotics for when they are truly needed. Safe.
